# Snowflake CLI

Snowflake CLI is an open-source command-line tool explicitly designed for developer-centric workloads in addition to SQL operations. It is a flexible and extensible tool that can accommodate modern development practices and technologies.

With Snowflake CLI, developers can create, manage, update, and view apps running on Snowflake across workloads such as Streamlit in Snowflake, the Snowflake Native App Framework, Snowpark Container Services, and Snowpark. It supports a range of Snowflake features, including user-defined functions, stored procedures, Streamlit in Snowflake, and SQL execution.

Docs: <https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-cli-v2/index>.

Quick start: <https://quickstarts.snowflake.com/guide/getting-started-with-snowflake-cli>

Cheatsheet: <https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/sf-cheatsheets/blob/main/snowflake-cli.md>


Feel free to file an issue or submit a PR here for general cases. For official support, contact Snowflake support at: https://community.snowflake.com/s/article/How-To-Submit-a-Support-Case-in-Snowflake-Lodge

`snow feedback` sends a rating and an optional note to Snowflake. Pass `--rating` from 1 (poor) to 4 (excellent). A note is optional for people and required for an AI agent: name the command you ran, what you expected, and what happened. Pass `--yes` when stdin is not a terminal. Do not include passwords, tokens, private keys, account locators, data from Snowflake accounts, or SQL that contains customer data.

## Install Snowflake CLI

### Direct install (recommended)

The direct installer downloads a signed platform binary from the Snowflake CLI repository and unpacks a versioned `snow` into your home directory.

macOS / Linux / WSL:

```bash
curl -LsS https://sfc-repo.snowflakecomputing.com/snowflake-cli/install.sh | sh
```

Windows (PowerShell):

```powershell
irm https://sfc-repo.snowflakecomputing.com/snowflake-cli/install.ps1 | iex
```

Pin a release with `--version` (or `SNOWFLAKE_CLI_VERSION`). Pass `--no-auto-upgrade` with a pin so later `snow` invocations do not replace it via auto-upgrade. This is the same flag as the root `snow --no-auto-upgrade`:

```bash
curl -LsS https://sfc-repo.snowflakecomputing.com/snowflake-cli/install.sh | sh -s -- --version 3.29.0 --no-auto-upgrade
```

```powershell
.\install.ps1 -Version 3.29.0 -NoAutoUpgrade
# or, without saving the script first:
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://sfc-repo.snowflakecomputing.com/snowflake-cli/install.ps1))) -Version 3.29.0 -NoAutoUpgrade
```

`irm ... | iex` cannot pass flags. With it, set `$env:SNOWFLAKE_CLI_VERSION` to pin a release. `--no-auto-upgrade` has no environment-variable form.

`--no-auto-upgrade` writes `auto_upgrade = false` under `[cli]` in the `config.toml` the CLI reads. If that file is a symlink, or has a `cli` table the installer cannot edit safely, the installer stops before installing and tells you what to add yourself.

Upgrade later with `snow upgrade` (same-major only). This is the only installer that supports it. `snow --info` reports `installation_source`; `snow --version` does not.

Auto-upgrade is off until you opt in, and it applies only to a direct install. Set `auto_upgrade = true` under `[cli]` in `config.toml`, or `SNOWFLAKE_CLI_AUTO_UPGRADE=1` for one process. Turn it off with `SNOWFLAKE_CLI_AUTO_UPGRADE=0`, `snow --no-auto-upgrade`, or the installer flag `--no-auto-upgrade`.

### Install with uv (PyPi)

Install Snowflake CLI in an isolated environment using [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/tools/#installing-tools). Requires Python >= 3.11. `snow upgrade` refuses on this channel.

```bash
uv tool install snowflake-cli
snow --help
```

Or, with a single command
```bash
uvx --from snowflake-cli snow --help
```

### Install with Homebrew (Mac only)

Requires [Homebrew](https://brew.sh/).

There are two ways to install Snowflake CLI via Homebrew:

**Option 1 – Homebrew core formula** (simpler, no tap required):

```bash
brew install snowflake-cli
snow --help
```

The formula is maintained by the Homebrew community and may trail the latest release.

**Option 2 – Snowflake-maintained tap (recommended for latest releases)**:

The tap distributes a pre-built binary (cask) maintained directly by Snowflake and updated with every release.
Homebrew requires you to explicitly trust third-party taps before installing casks from them:

```bash
brew tap snowflakedb/snowflake-cli
brew trust --cask snowflakedb/snowflake-cli/snowflake-cli
brew install --cask snowflake-cli
snow --help
```

Once trusted, future upgrades work normally: `brew upgrade --cask snowflake-cli`

### Install from source

Requires Python >= 3.11 and git

```bash
git clone https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-cli
cd snowflake-cli
# you can also do the below in an active virtual environment:
# python -m venv .venv
# source .venv/bin/activate
hatch build && pip install .
snow --version
```

You should now be able to run `snow` and get the CLI message.

## Customize the SQL REPL prompt

The interactive `snow sql` prompt remains ` > ` unless you opt in with
`--prompt-format` or a quoted `prompt_format` string in the `[cli]` section of
`config.toml`. Placeholders (case-insensitive) are `[user]`, `[host]`,
`[account]`, `[role]`, `[warehouse]`, `[database]`, `[schema]`, and
`[connection]` (the `-c` connection name). They update after `USE`. Example:

```
snow sql --prompt-format "[user]#[warehouse]@[database].[schema]> "
```

Missing values render as `(no user)`, `(no database)`, and so on.
`\n` is a newline; `\[`, `\]`, and `\\` are literal `[`, `]`, and `\`.
Use `[#rrggbb]` for a foreground colour and `[bg:#rrggbb]` for a background
colour. A colour applies to the prompt text that follows it; it does not colour
SQL input. Quote the value because `#` starts a TOML comment. For example:

```toml
[cli]
prompt_format = """┌──[#bca81f][user]@[account].[role].[warehouse].[database].[schema]
[#ffff00]└─$"""
```

SnowSQL often puts a colour after the marker (`└─$[#ffff00]`). Here that
trailing token is a no-op: it does not colour typed SQL. Place `[#ffff00]`
before `└─$` if you want the marker itself yellow.

Unknown bracketed tokens are dropped from the prompt and reported with a
warning when the REPL starts. Prefix a colour directive with `\[` to display
it literally.

## Default output format

Commands print a table unless you pass `--format`. To change that default, set
`output_format` in the `[cli]` section of `config.toml` or the
`SNOWFLAKE_CLI_OUTPUT_FORMAT` environment variable. Allowed values are `TABLE`,
`JSON`, `JSON_EXT`, `CSV`, and `PLAIN`. `--format` on the command line still wins.
In `snow sql`, `!set output_format=<format>` changes the format for later
statements in that session. `!set timing=false` hides the `Time Elapsed` line
that follows each statement. `!set timing_in_output_file=true` also writes that
line into a file opened with `!spool`. Both accept `true`, `yes`, `on`, and `1`,
or `false`, `no`, `off`, and `0`. An empty value is rejected and leaves the
current setting unchanged. `timing` is on by default and
`timing_in_output_file` is off, so a spool file keeps the results only. JSON,
JSON_EXT, and CSV output never include the line. `!set echo=true` prints each
statement before its result, on the terminal and in an open `!spool` file. The
default is `echo=false`. JSON, JSON_EXT, and CSV stay free of that statement so
the result stays parseable. One `!set` changes one option.
`!set output_file=<path>` opens the same file as `!spool <path>`, and
`!spool off` closes it. To spool from the start of a run, pass
`-o output_file=<path>`.
To hide query results on the terminal from the start of a run, pass
`-o quiet=true`. It accepts the same values as `!set quiet`, and an open
spool file still receives the results.
To set the output format from the start of a run, pass
`-o output_format=<format>`. It accepts the same names as
`!set output_format` and overrides the `output_format` config key and the
`SNOWFLAKE_CLI_OUTPUT_FORMAT` variable. It cannot be combined with `--format`:
passing both is an error and no SQL runs. `!set output_format` can still
change the format later.

```toml
[cli]
output_format = "JSON"
```

## Get involved

Have a feature idea? Running into a bug? Want to contribute? We'd love to hear from you!
Please open or review issues, open pull requests, or reach out to us on <developers@snowflake.com>

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and contribution guidelines.
